BARBELL_SQUAT.name: Squat
BARBELL_SQUAT.description: The Squat is the king of all exercises. Squats work the whole body: Your legs bend and straighten to move the weight; your abs and lower back muscles stabilize your trunk while your legs move; your upper back, shoulders and arms balance the bar on your back
goodForm: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned out about 30°
Big breath and brace your abs before every rep
Push your knees out in line with your toes
Sit down until your hip crease is below the top of your knees
Keep the bar over the middle of your foot
Drive your hips up and keep your chest up
badForm: Let your knees cave inward
Lift your heels off the floor
Stop above parallel
Round or over-arch your lower back
Let the bar drift forward over your toes

DEADLIFT.name: Deadlift
DEADLIFT.description: The “dead” in Deadlift stands for dead weight. So every rep must start on the floor, from a dead stop. You don’t Deadlift top-down like on the Squat or Bench Press. You start at the bottom, pull the weight up and then return it to the floor
goodForm: Bar over the middle of your foot, shins a few centimetres away
Grip just outside your legs, arms straight
Bend your knees until your shins touch the bar
Lift your chest to flatten your back, then breathe and brace
Drag the bar up your legs
Finish standing tall with hips and knees locked
badForm: Let your hips shoot up before the bar moves
Round your lower back
Let the bar drift away from your legs
Lean back or shrug at the top
Bounce the bar off the floor between reps
Jerk the bar off the floor

BENCH_PRESS.name: Bench press
BENCH_PRESS.description: Bench-press is a full body compound exercise that works your chest, shoulders and triceps. The bench press is the most effective exercise for upper-body strength.
goodForm: Lie with your eyes under the bar
Grip a bit wider than shoulders, thumbs around the bar
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, feet planted
Lower to your lower chest with forearms vertical
Touch your chest on every rep
Press back up over your shoulders to straight arms
badForm: Use a thumbless grip
Flare your elbows straight out to the sides
Bounce the bar off your chest
Lift your hips off the bench
Let your wrists bend far back

MILITARY_PRESS.name: Overhead press
MILITARY_PRESS.description: The Overhead Press is a full body, compound exercise. Your shoulders and arms press the weight over your head while your legs, lower back and abs balance you. The Overhead Press is one of the best exercises to build strong, muscular and healthy shoulders with bigger arms.
goodForm: Grip just outside your shoulders, bar in the heel of your palm
Elbows slightly in front of the bar
Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs
Move your face back and press the bar straight up
Lock your elbows with the bar over your mid-foot
Shrug up into the bar at the top
badForm: Bend your knees to drive the bar (that is a push press)
Lean back excessively
Let your wrists fold backwards
Press the bar forward around your face
Start with your elbows behind the bar

CHINUPS.name: Chin-up
CHINUPS.description: Pullups (and chin-ups) are hard because you have to lift your entire body weight on day one. If you can't do one chin-up, do negatives: Climb up to the top position, and lift yourself down. Everybody is stronger on the way down, so you can do this. When you can do 10 good form negatives, you can do one chin-up.
goodForm: Grip with palms facing you, about shoulder-width
Start each rep from a dead hang, arms straight
Pull your elbows down toward your ribs
Get your chin over the bar
Lower under control back to straight arms
badForm: Kip or swing your legs
Do half reps
Drop into the bottom uncontrolled
Crane your neck to reach the bar

CURLS.name: Barbell curl
goodForm: Stand tall, underhand grip at shoulder width
Keep your elbows pinned at your sides
Curl until your forearms are vertical
Lower under control to straight arms
badForm: Swing the bar with your hips or back
Let your elbows drift forward
Lean back to finish the rep
Cut the bottom of the movement short

CRUNCHES.name: Weighted crunches
goodForm: Lie with knees bent and feet flat
Hold the weight against your chest
Curl your ribs toward your pelvis, lifting your shoulder blades
Breathe out on the way up
Lower slowly
badForm: Pull on your neck
Sit all the way up using your hip flexors
Use momentum
Hold your breath

BENT_OVER_ROW.name: Barbell row
BENT_OVER_ROW.description: Barbell Rows are a full body, compound exercise. They work your upper-back, lower back, hips and arms. They build a stronger, muscular back and bigger biceps. Barbell Rows are one of the most effective assistance exercises you can do to increase your Squat, Bench Press and Deadlift.
goodForm: Stand with the bar over your mid-foot, deadlift-width grip
Hinge forward with a flat back, torso near parallel to the floor
Pull the bar to your upper belly, elbows leading
Lower the bar under control each rep
badForm: Stand up as you pull
Round your back
Jerk the weight with your legs
Shorten the range of motion

DIPS.name: Dips
DIPS.description: Dips are a compound, body-weight exercise. You do Dips by first raising yourself on two dip bars with straight arms. Lower your body until your shoulders are below your elbows. Push yourself up until your arms are straight again. Dips work your chest, shoulders, back and arm muscles.
goodForm: Start at the top with elbows locked
Lean slightly forward, shoulders down and back
Lower until your shoulders are just below your elbows
Keep your elbows tracking back
Press back up to full lockout
badForm: Shrug your shoulders toward your ears
Flare your elbows wide
Bounce at the bottom
Go deeper than your shoulders tolerate
Swing your legs

INCLINE_BENCH_PRESS.name: Incline bench press
goodForm: Set the bench to a low incline, about 30°
Plant your feet and keep your shoulder blades against the bench
Lower the bar to your upper chest with wrists over elbows
Press smoothly with your hips on the bench
badForm: Flare your elbows straight out
Bounce the bar off your chest
Lift your hips off the bench
Bend your wrists back under the bar

ROMANIAN_DEADLIFT.name: Romanian deadlift
goodForm: Start standing with the bar close to your thighs
Soften your knees and push your hips back
Lower the bar along your legs with your back neutral
Stand by driving your hips forward
badForm: Round your lower back
Squat down instead of hinging at the hips
Reach for the floor after your hips stop moving
Let the bar drift away from your legs

LEG_PRESS.name: Leg press
goodForm: Keep your back and hips against the pad
Place your feet about shoulder-width apart
Lower only as far as your pelvis stays against the pad
Press through your whole foot with knees tracking over toes
badForm: Lift your hips off the pad
Let your knees collapse inward
Bounce out of the bottom
Snap your knees back at the top

LEG_CURL.name: Leg curl
goodForm: Line your knees up with the machine pivot
Set the roller just above your heels
Curl smoothly with your hips against the pad
Lower slowly through a comfortable range
badForm: Lift your hips to move the weight
Jerk the weight up
Drop the weight on the way down
Force a range that causes knee pain

CALF_RAISE.name: Calf raise
goodForm: Place the balls of your feet securely on the platform
Keep your knees steady throughout the rep
Raise your heels as high as you comfortably can
Lower slowly into a comfortable calf stretch
badForm: Bounce at the bottom
Roll your ankles outward
Bend and straighten your knees to lift
Rush through short reps

LAT_PULLDOWN.name: Lat pulldown
goodForm: Secure your thighs under the pad
Sit tall with a small backward lean
Pull your elbows down as the bar approaches your upper chest
Return slowly until your arms extend comfortably
badForm: Pull the bar behind your neck
Swing your torso to move the weight
Shrug throughout the pull
Release the weight suddenly

SEATED_CABLE_ROW.name: Seated cable row
goodForm: Sit tall with your feet braced and knees slightly bent
Pull the handle toward your lower ribs
Move your shoulder blades smoothly as your elbows travel back
Return slowly with your torso steady
badForm: Rock your torso back and forth
Round your lower back
Shrug your shoulders toward your ears
Jerk the handle to start the pull

TRICEP_PUSHDOWN.name: Triceps pushdown
goodForm: Stand tall with your elbows close to your sides
Keep your upper arms still
Straighten your elbows smoothly
Return slowly without letting your elbows drift forward
badForm: Swing your shoulders to move the weight
Lean your whole body onto the handle
Flare your elbows out
Let the weight stack slam down

DUMBBELL_ROW.name: One-arm dumbbell row
goodForm: Brace your free hand on a stable bench
Keep your back neutral and hips level
Pull your elbow toward your hip
Lower slowly until your arm extends comfortably
badForm: Twist your torso to lift
Round your lower back
Shrug the weight toward your ear
Drop the dumbbell between reps

DB_SHOULDER_PRESS.name: Dumbbell shoulder press
goodForm: Sit with your back supported and feet planted
Start with the dumbbells near shoulder height
Press up with wrists over elbows
Lower slowly through a comfortable range
badForm: Over-arch your lower back
Bang the dumbbells together overhead
Bend your wrists back
Force your shoulders through a painful range

DB_LATERAL_RAISE.name: Dumbbell lateral raise
goodForm: Stand tall with a slight bend in your elbows
Raise your arms out to the sides to a comfortable height
Keep your wrists neutral and shoulders relaxed
Lower the dumbbells slowly
badForm: Swing your torso for momentum
Shrug your shoulders toward your ears
Turn your thumbs sharply down
Drop the weights on the way down

SIDELYING_EXTERNAL_ROTATION.name: Side-lying external rotation
goodForm: Lie on your side with your top elbow bent 90° against your ribs
Keep your shoulder blade steady as you rotate your forearm upward
Lift and lower slowly with your elbow staying at your side
Use your full pain-free range
badForm: Roll your torso backward to lift
Let your elbow drift away from your ribs
Shrug or lose shoulder blade control
Rush the rep or push through pain

PRONE_HORIZONTAL_ABDUCTION.name: Prone horizontal abduction
goodForm: Lie face down with your arm hanging from a stable bench
Raise your arm out to the side with a slight elbow bend
Guide your shoulder blade smoothly as you lift and lower slowly
Use your full pain-free range with your neck relaxed
badForm: Twist your torso to lift
Shrug toward your ear
Drop your arm on the way down
Force the arm beyond a pain-free range

PRONE_EXTERNAL_ROTATION.name: Prone external rotation at 90°
goodForm: Lie face down with your upper arm supported out to the side at 90°
Bend your elbow 90° and let your forearm hang down
Keep your shoulder blade steady as you rotate up and lower slowly
Use your full pain-free range without lifting your elbow
badForm: Lift your elbow off its support
Arch your back to move the weight
Shrug or lose shoulder blade control
Rush the movement or push through pain

SUPINE_PROTRACTION.name: Supine scapular protraction
goodForm: Lie on your back with the dumbbell above your shoulder
Keep your elbow straight without forcing it backward
Reach slowly toward the ceiling, then lower your shoulder blade with control
Use your full pain-free range with your torso still
badForm: Bend your elbow to move the weight
Roll your whole torso off the bench
Shrug your shoulder toward your ear
Drop your shoulder back or push through pain

SCAPTION.name: Seated elevation in the scapular plane
goodForm: Sit tall with your arms slightly forward of your sides
Keep your thumbs pointing up as you raise your arms
Let your shoulder blades move smoothly as you lift and lower slowly
Use your full pain-free range without leaning back
badForm: Swing your torso for momentum
Shrug your shoulders toward your ears
Turn your thumbs down as you lift
Rush the lowering or force a painful range
